drug_class: Cholesterol-lowering combination (ATP-citrate lyase inhibitor + cholesterol absorption inhibitor)
purpose: This medicine is used to lower your 'bad' cholesterol (LDL) levels in your blood. It is often prescribed for adults who cannot take statins or need extra help lowering their cholesterol. Keeping cholesterol under control helps reduce your risk of heart attack and stroke.
how_it_works: This pill combines two medicines that work in two different ways to lower your cholesterol. Bempedoic acid works in your liver to slow down the production of cholesterol in your body. Ezetimibe works in your gut to block the absorption of cholesterol from the food you eat, so less cholesterol gets into your bloodstream.
common_side_effects: Some people may notice upper respiratory infections (like a cold), muscle or joint pain, stomach pain, tiredness, back pain, or a rise in uric acid levels (which can trigger gout). Abnormal liver enzyme levels have also been reported.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney problems, or a history of gout, as this medicine can raise uric acid and make gout worse. Avoid taking it if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. It can interact with certain other medications, so always tell your doctor and pharmacist about everything else you are taking. Regular blood tests may be needed to check your liver and uric acid levels.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one tablet taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
